utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The first witness is going to seek a measure of protection. May I address that in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over the page, paragraph 7. You can deal with the build-up of events, if asked and if permitted, but I'm not going to trouble you with those because they've been dealt with by other witnesses. Did you attend any meetings in the presence of either Anto Valenta or Pero Skopljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was present on one occasion at a meeting where Mr. Anto Valenta was present and also once when Mr. Pero Skopljak was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I touch on either of those meetings, had you read Valenta's book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had read the book written by Mr. Valenta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, I think, are a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm a Bosniak of Islamic faith.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To you, when you read the book at the time, how did it seem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time, the book seemed to me to be unusual, because it dealt with an issue which, until that time, had not been addressed in that area, that is, the issue of a peaceful division leading to togetherness. The book was conceived in such a way that it was based on the ethnic principle of division, division of the existing administrative territories of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Reading through the book, it did not anticipate the events that would follow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, after the events, with hindsight, how does the book now seem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Later on, developments showed that the book envisaged a scenario on the basis of which many things developed in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and particularly within the area of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The meeting with either or both of these men that you attended, tell us about that or those. When did the meeting or meetings occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A meeting was first held in the so-called hunting lodge, where an attempt was made to ease tensions between the Bosniak and Croatian peoples, and to continue to work together in preparing the defence from the aggression. I was not present at that prior meeting because, at the time, I was not a member of any political party but was a member of the coordinating board for the protection of the interests of Muslims. I was invited to a second meeting to the fire brigade centre in Vitez, where again joint activities were discussed and when, for the first time -- I don't know whether it was the first time, but we did discuss the formation of a joint army within the territory of Vitez municipality, and reference was made to Mr. Franjo Nakic as a joint commander of that future unit which was to defend the area of Vitez. A second time I attended a meeting was the one held in the post office in Vitez. I was visiting my father, who was ill, and I was looking for a doctor to come and examine him. However, he was absent. When those events occurred I was with my father, and mister --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That meeting was held in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What part of 1992, what month?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One moment, please. There's a problem with the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I understand five or ten minutes are required to put the matter right. We'll rise. --- Break taken at 9.55 a.m.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the clarity of the debate, I wish to point out that we are in public session since page 10, line 12, of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we'll go on now till half past 11. We'll take only a quarter of an hour break and then go on until 1.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness N, you were telling us about the meeting in 1992; can you help us with the month when the meeting occurred that you were telling us about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That meeting was held either at the end of October, between the 20th and maybe the 1st or 2nd of November, roughly in that period of time, and it was held in the Vitez post office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was there for the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, the meeting was attended by Mr. Pero Skopljak, Mr. Mario Cerkez, Zvonko Cilic, Marko Knezevic. That would be the names that I can recollect as people attending.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that there was a meeting when Valenta was present. Was it at this meeting, or another meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Valenta, as I said a moment ago, was present at the meeting held in the fire brigade centre in Stari Vitez. I don't remember him attending this meeting in the post office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the post office meeting, was an order that Rajic had raised discussed, or an order that Rajic had made discussed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As Mr. Rajic was then appointed Minister of Defence in Bosnia-Herzegovina, so there was a discussion -- I don't know whether you'd call it an order, in military structures, but it was a document which ordered that units which in those days constituted the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina -- or rather units of the Territorial Defence -- in the municipalities in which the Croatian Democratic Union had won a majority at the democratic elections, should be placed under the command of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was discussed; what was the resolution of that part of the discussion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This first discussion I could describe as having born no fruit, because the Croatian side insisted that this document be adopted, whereas the Bosniak side insisted that the joint document remain in force, and there was even a proposal made that if armies are united, that both insignia be worn -- that is, of the HVO and of the BH army: that on one sleeve the HVO be worn, that is, the chequerboard flag, and on the other sleeve, the lily insignia. This was not accepted, and the meeting ended in such a way that, due to the fact the most responsible people from the SDA had not attended, it was agreed that the meeting be postponed, that consultations be held on the ground regarding that issue, and that is how the meeting ended. I did not participate in subsequent talks and meetings. If I may explain a little, how it happened that I was present at that meeting --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may become relevant, but I don't seek that material from you at the moment. In any event, remember, we're keeping your anonymity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the meeting concerned at all to stop shooting that was going on at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that meeting, as there had been incidents prior to the meeting, there had been an incident in Ahmici, so the question was raised at the meeting as to how to stop such incidents and avoid any repetition in other parts. However, this issue attracted very little time. Of course, I didn't join in in the discussion on that issue because I was not a military man; I had not even served in the military, so I didn't take part in the discussion on that issue at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The next meeting, the follow-up meeting, was scheduled for how long hence? How much later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the meeting in the post office?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was scheduled for two or three days later. I think the deadline of two or three days was given, that we should have consultations on the ground, and then another meeting should be held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did Dr. Mujezinovic attend the follow-up meeting, you not attending it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, he did attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of the attitude being taken, was the coordination committee formed? "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The coordination committee had been formed earlier on, sometime in July 1992 or the beginning of August. Its task was to explain to the people what was happening and to protect the interests of the Bosniak people, in the sense that -- in other areas, not the military, because the Territorial Defence and the army already existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the coordination committee have any military functions or was it purely civilian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a purely civilian body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it make efforts to return to official BiH government, by the use of flags and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As the legally elected government, the one elected at the first democratic elections, the president of the executive board and two members of the executive board were Bosniaks. As an executive body, it functioned and it made proposals to the coordination committee and the SDA how to re-establish unified government in the area of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the HVO response to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The response is well known. The efforts did not bear fruit, and from then on until the Dayton Agreement, or until the first post-war joint elections in the Federation, there were parallel governments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I think we've heard about these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We could go on to April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I just touch on paragraph 14. So throughout the time that you were aware of what was going on, were civil and military authority within the HVO/HZ-HB separated in any way, one from the other, or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was united under the name the Croatian Defence Council. It combined both civilian and military authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think there was a family birthday, again you needn't give the date because of anonymity, but there was a family birthday on the 15th of April, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you indeed celebrate that birthday that evening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, at some stage that day, see some of a television broadcast in the form of a press conference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to look at two tapes that show that broadcast, and we're going to look at it from start to finish, but in order to fix the event in your mind and to see what help you can give us as to the timing of the broadcast, at some stage does a doctor feature on one or other of these tapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. A doctor was seen, with his back turned, when he was doing an on-site inspection into an incident when Mr. Totic had been captured or attacked, whatever you like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the doctor somebody who -- again, don't say how -- but was it somebody you either knew or recognised by sound or sight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I personally did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you concentrate on all of the television broadcast or only on a part of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only a part of it. The routine part with the report saying this and that had happened, we didn't follow that with any attention. However, when it was announced that Mr. Kordic and Mr. Kostroman were to speak -- I don't know the names of the other speakers. I never met Mr. Kordic in person myself, but since he was a well-known figure in the Lasva Valley, he would appear frequently on television, even though he completed his secondary education in Vitez. We are of a different generation, so we didn't have occasion to meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can now play both tapes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I must explain to the witness that we're going to play the tapes continuously without asking you questions about them as they're being played, because for technical reasons it's much easier to play the tapes continuously. Will you be good enough to look at them and listen to them as they're played, and I'll ask you some questions about them afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So if the booth could very kindly play the first tape. We, therefore, have Exhibit 665.3 to hand.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "This morning, four persons were killed, the escort, Ivica Vidovic; Anto Zrnic; Marko and Tihomir Ljubic; and a civilian. "According to the police report, he was probably an eyewitness. The commander of the brigade, Zivko Totic, was kidnapped and taken in an unknown direction. "The driver, three escorts and one civilian. "Can we look at the videotapes of that event."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We can move on. We can fast forward this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. If the booth could fast forward then to the time when the -- I'm not sure whether the Chamber intended to fast forward this passage. This is the -- some of the list, but we can probably pick it up with the translation, if the booth would be good enough.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "4th of March, 1993, members of MOS stopped a bus in Zepca, searched it and demanded to see the identity papers of the passengers for no reason. "On 28th February, members of MOS checked vehicles in Travnik. They appropriated a pistol and shot at two passenger vehicles. "On 7th March, near the village of Ahmici in Vitez, which is inhabited by Muslims, shots were fired at a building in which an active platoon of military police was stationed. "On 9th March, in the village of Visnjica in Zenica, five members of the army of BH entered the house of Milko Kristo, ransacked the place and looted everything in it, finally setting fire to the house. "On 15th March, near the "Maks" shop in Vitez, members of the BH army threw a hand grenade, wounding one person, a woman, and child. There was major material damage. "On 16th March, in the village of Dolac, municipality of Travnik, Zoran Matosevic and Ivo Juric, who were members of the Travnik HVO, were killed by Mujahedins. "On 16th March, Drago Mitrovic from Zenica was stopped and 7.000 German marks were taken from him. "On 17th of March, the houses of Milorad and Vlatko Tvrtkovic were broken into and everything in them was taken away. "On 17th of March, Zaim Vukovic, a member of the BH army, was arrested in Zenica for attempting to break into an HVO vehicle. "On 17th of March, a little girl, Gordana Rados, was seriously wounded in Kakanj. The shots came from positions of the BH army. "On 17th March, the command of the Kakanj HOS, Ivo Vuletic, was killed in Kakanj. He was killed by Sakib, a member of the Kakanj MUP. "On 17th of March, members of the army of BH threw a hand grenade at the premises of the Travnik military police. "On 16th of March, a member of the army of BH threw a hand grenade at the HVO military commander, Donja Veceriska. "On 15th of March, a member of the BH army fired shots from an infantry weapon at the HVO commander, Donja Veceriska. "On 22nd of March, members of the MUP and the BH army removed licence plates bearing the insignia of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna from vehicles at all checkpoints in Zenica. "On 23rd of March, in the village of Kacuni, municipality of Busovaca, members of the BH army appropriated an FAP 18 freight vehicle from Vitez which was carrying humanitarian aid to Brestovsko. "On 23rd of March, members of the BH army shot at the building of the military police in Travnik from a freight vehicle. "On 23rd of March, members of the BH army shot at the building of the military police in Travnik from firearms at the sanatorium on the same day --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we have enough to get a picture of that. We have the other items clearly before us. We can read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, and the speed of delivery is placing, I think, quite a strain on the interpreters as well as the LiveNote recorders, and we can, I think, be confident from the interpretation so far that the transcript on Z665.3 appears to be entirely accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So if we now move to the second tape, please, and if the Chamber and my friends turn to what is marked as page 18, I hope I've got this tape to start at about the 25th of March, with Stjepan Radic, and it may be that the first real entry will be the 17th of January. It comes from a different viewpoint. Once we are under way, may I sit down?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "On 17th January, members of the BH army killed Srecko Weber, the HVO military policemen in Travnik. "In Travnik, on 5 January, members of the BH army stopped Franjo, robbed him, and forced him to shoot himself, taking his own life. "On the 9th, several members of the BH army opened fire at the premises of the HVO in Novi Travnik. "On 21 January, members of the BH army opened fire on Croatian houses in Kruscica, municipality of Vitez. On the same day, members of the BH army stopped two military policemen in Stari Vitez, mistreated them, and swore at them. "On 10 September, 1992, members of the BH army took Ivica Polak, the commander of the Travnik HVO from Travnik. "On 10 September, members of the BH army murdered Ante Cepina, a taxi driver in Novi Travnik. "On 12 February, 1993, members of the BH army from Vitez murdered Sasa Jurisic. "On 24 February, members of the BH army killed a member of the military police and a civilian in Busovaca. "On 14 April, members of the BH army fired four shells from a mortar in the direction of Pucisevo from Travnik. "On 17 January, members of the BH army disarmed 17 members of the HVO in Kruscici, Municipality of Vitez. "You have heard about today's events. "This was an overview of the incidents caused by the members of the BH army since February 27, 1993. "The commander of the Operative Zone in Central Bosnia has issued an announcement to the Croatian population and the general population. It will be read by Mr. Marko Prskalo, the assistant commander for the brigade. "MR. PRSKALO: Announcement: The Muslim extremist forces, which are under the command of the 3rd Corps of the BH army, led by Enver Hadzihasanovic, have activated a plan to murder officers and leaders of the HVO on the territory of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. Their intentions are clear: to cause a widespread conflict between the BH army and the HVO, to destroy the HVO and prevent the implementation of the Vance-Owen peace accord signed in New York, providing for the establishment of provinces. Those who call themselves members of the BH army are burning Croatian flags just before Easter, threatening Croats, looting, killing Croatian officers and kidnapping people, and yet they talk to us about a joint fight against the Chetniks, while doing nothing about the misdeeds except distancing themselves. In these difficult moments in the history of the Croats, we call upon the Croatian people and the members of the HVO to be resolute in defending our territories and our homes. We have the strength to deal with any enemy who attacks us. We condemn the terrorist behaviour of the extremist Muslim forces, and in the interest of peace, we demand that all Mujahedins be expelled from our territory. The command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. "JOURNALIST: Thank you very much. Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, you have the microphone. "TIHOMIR BLASKIC: Ladies and gentlemen, I would like to greet you on behalf of the command of the Operative Zone and on my own behalf. I would like to express my condolences to the families and relatives of our soldiers of the Croatian Defence Council who have been killed, soldiers who honourably carried out their tasks and gave what was most valuable possessions, that is, who gave what every soldier of the Croatian Defence Council is prepared give, i.e., their lives. In our struggle against the enemy, the enemy first of all of the Croatian people, it is certainly our duty to deal with that enemy in a civilised way, as befits every soldier of the Croatian Defence Council. I think there is no doubt, as is evident from the announcement, that the responsibility for all these crimes perpetrated against the Croatian people rests with the command of the 3rd Corps, headed by the commander of the 3rd Corps, because it is this command which gave the order for the shelling of the Croatian territories at Puticevo last night, in the immediate vicinity of the main intersection leading to Novi Travnik, Vitez, and Travnik, and the shelling was carried out, as has been documented, from the facilities and military positions of the BH army in the old town of Travnik. It is also evident that the perpetrators of all the acts committed up to now were mostly members of the 7th Muslim Brigade, an extremist brigade, which is irked by anyone who is not a religious fanatic, and which is part of the 3rd Corps of the BH army headed by the commander of the 3rd Corps, Enver Hadzihasanovic. The list of crimes is certainly much, much longer. We have also received information reports from the leading people in the command that the holiday, today's holiday on 15 April, will be celebrated in a warlike manner. We expected it to be celebrated in a warlike manner in the fight against the common aggressor, that is, against the Chetniks, and not in a fight against the Croatian people, against the officers of the Croatian people and the sons of the Croatian people who are also fighting the Chetniks and the common enemy. The murder in Travnik was only the beginning of this dirty scenario. Although evidence has been presented, the entire procedure completed and conclusions signed regarding a trial, it is certain that somebody did not find it fit to bring to justice those who butchered the commander of the Travnik Brigade, Colonel Stojak, and who perpetrated a number of other acts. You have been informed only about some of these acts today. The burning of Croatian flags in Travnik on the Catholic holiday, on Good Friday, and throughout the Easter holidays, is also an indication of the extent to which they are committed to a joint command and fellowship. I believe that the Croatian people in these territories, the Lasva region and beyond, as well as international public opinion, have had an opportunity to learn about this vandalism, because they celebrated these acts and they flaunted a number of flags which they had burned and riddled with bullets. It is very likely that today certain individuals, together with perpetrators of this terrible crime and butchery in Zenica this morning, are celebrating their success, presided over by those who issued such commands. This is yet another step to their achieving their goal. I would like to tell the Muslim people that they should be aware of the gravity of these acts and the historical responsibility to which they are being pushed by this kind of leadership, headed by this kind of command. The announcement to the Croatian people should serve to convince the Croatian people, as it certainly will, although they are already aware of these events, that all the institutions of the HVO still have the strength and the ability to deal with such terrorists, such criminals here in this territory. It is also a signal that in every place, at every time, these criminals should be told in public that we do not need them in our territory because criminals of any nation are unwelcome on any territory. I have already said that last night we received not just a report but a military combat order that fire should be opened on the Croatian area of Puticevo from 60 and 82 millimetre mortars. Those to whom the command was issued did carry it out, as the citizens of Travnik know full well. I think that after this, there is no need for any special comments regarding any negotiations with such representatives and with this kind of leadership of the 3rd Corps, which has obviously come here to liberate this territory from the Croats, rather than from the Chetniks, because up to now, they have not liberated an inch of territory from the Chetniks at the front line. A number of other measures which are to follow are intended to let everyone know that members of such units, who have committed such heinous crimes, are not welcome in this territory. This is also to let all the soldiers of the Croatian Defence Council know that they should treat the enemy according to the instructions they have been given. That's all. "JOURNALIST: Thank you, Colonel. Mr. Dario Kordic, you have the floor. "DARIO KORDIC: Ladies and gentlemen, you have seen and heard a lot of things today. I do not wish to repeat some of these things. I think that every normal person would find the pictures we have seen today deeply moving. The Croatian people from this area find them especially moving, because they constitute a clear message as to what the extremist Muslim forces want. According to their plans, there should be no Croatian territory, and that there should be no Croatian people or Croatian Defence Council in the region. Along with my condolences to the families of the Croatian Defence Council defenders who have been killed, I would like to send a message to the Croatian people that we are more united than ever and that we are ready to finally fend off all enemy attacks. These are the crucial days, crucial moments for the defence of the Croatian territories of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Therefore, all those who want to turn their weapons against the Croatian people should know that the Croatian people are ready to respond to any such attempt. What has happened today is clearly an open declaration of war against the Croatian people, against the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, by the extremist Muslim forces. But unfortunately we cannot say this is only the extremist Muslim forces, because evidently the entire leadership of the 3rd Muslim Corps is backing the 7th Muslim Brigade which has been pushed into the foreground to perpetrate atrocities and commit assassinations and terrorist acts, since you yourselves have seen that, sadly, over 20 young men, defenders, have recently lost their lives in a detestable and bestial manner, treacherously killed by the enemy, the Muslim extremists. They have thus demonstrated clearly what kind of strategy they wish to adopt at this time. They want to cause unrest among the Croatian people by assassinating their leaders, brigade commanders, politician and so on. I think that they have achieved quite the opposite, that the Croatian people are more resolute, more unified than ever. We would like to tell the Croatian people that there is no cause for anxiety or concern. I'm sure that the units of the Croatian Defence Council are doing everything that is necessary even as we speak. I'm certain that a plan has been made and that the units are in full combat readiness. This is also clear to our opponents who have set out to attack this Croatian territory. I would like this opportunity to call upon the people living in our territories and that the part of the Muslim people who live here on the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna not to join these extremists, not to be led by those insane ideas, those who are leading them to their deaths, to evil, and to stay safe here with the Croatian people who have nothing against the Muslim people, but who are against those who are turning their rifles against the Croats. It must be clear to everyone today what is going on and who is perpetrating an aggression on this territory. I think that things have gone far enough. Even more, you are witnessing the fact that last night and today a very serious act of aggression by the Muslim forces is taking place against the Croatian territory of Konjic, where a large part of the Croatian population is fleeing, where atrocities have been committed in Buturovic Polje, where the Croatian people are going through a terrible agony in the Konjic municipality and where the government of the Croatian Defence Council sent a clear message to everyone at its special meeting yesterday that units of the Croatian Defence Council are ready to repel all the attacks on this integral part of the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Certainly what is happening today shows that they are using this day, which is ostensibly a day of celebration of this Muslim army, to give a message to the Croatian people when they least expected it. I think we should conclude by saying that the Croatian people should now show their real strength and that in the days to come, we shall transform the psychological stability we have into a final victory and the survival of the Croatian people in this region. Thank you. "JOURNALIST: Thank you, Mr. Vice-president. I would now like Mr. Ignac Kostroman to say something. "IGNAC KOSTROMAN: Today, on the anniversary of the establishment and organisation of the Muslim forces or the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the 3rd Corps of this same army of Bosnia and Herzegovina is celebrating with a bloodbath. What other word can we use to describe this celebration of their anniversary when, as the previous speakers have pointed out, they have not liberated an inch of this territory. This army is watching as the helpless people of eastern Bosnia are dying and suffering, and instead of turning against the aggressor, they have turned against their closest allies, the Croatian people and the units of the Croatian Defence Council. So far, we have been extremely tolerant and extremely patient. Now when you see the chronology of all these events, you will see that we have always tried to resolve all problems by talks, and that we have tried to reason with at least the sound part of the forces in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Unfortunately, however, the situation worsened daily. When the Muslim forces saw that they could not occupy our territory by open aggression, they embarked on terrorist acts with the main goal of assassinating the leaders, to disorient the Croatian people, to kill them, destroy them, and drive them out of this region. The latest crime perpetrated against the commander of the brigade in Zenica, Mr. Totic, whose fate is still unknown, shows that this extremist part of the Muslim forces will not give up their plan. On this very day, with the way in which they are celebrating their anniversary, they are showing that, according to their plans, they see us as worse enemies and opponents than the Chetnik forces who have occupied over 60 per cent of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. We made efforts to calm down the Croatian people and the military units. This was our duty and our right, especially as we are in the key positions and the people were looking to us for guidance. In these difficult and fateful times, we again would like to send a message to the Croatian people that we shall do what we believe is the most reasonable course of action for all the people living in this territory. We shall not be the first to retaliate anywhere, but where a single Croat is imperilled, is threatened, we shall defend him as is our right and respond with all the means available to us. Therefore, we are still leaving some room for those Muslim forces who are reasonable in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to reconsider their actions and to bring the war criminals to justice. If they do not want to do it, we shall have enough strength and means to bring all these war criminals to trial before the people, starting with Enver Hadzihasanovic, and Sefer Halilovic, who is directly commanding the forces in Konjic, causing destruction on the Croatian territory. We would like to end today's discussion with the following messages: The people should have confidence in us. At this time, which is fateful for the Croatian people in this territory, we would like to send a message that no one should do anything on their own initiative because there is a military command here which will take certain steps to protect the Croats in this territory. "JOURNALIST: The staff in Mostar, with regard to the latest events and more or less what the intentions are. "TIHOMIR BLASKIC: The chief of the main staff and the main staff in Mostar and that line of defence have been informed of all this, including this morning's crime which occurred, and members of the Croatian Defence Council are being kept informed of everything that is going on. As I have just said, regardless of the gravity of this, we shall treat the enemy as required by the system of control and command. So all the institutions of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna have been informed of this massacre that has occurred and of all the events that followed, especially what was done by the extremist section of the Muslim forces. The measures that will be taken will certainly be aimed primarily at protecting the Croatian people, because one of the tasks of the Croatian Defence Council is certainly to defend the territory and protect the people where they live. "DARIO KORDIC: Perhaps, in the spirit of your question, we should say what is happening right now shows that it is the intention of the Muslim forces not only to work directly against the Croatian people but also to directly undermine the Vance-Owen Plan, which has been signed by their president too. His signature obviously means nothing either to him or to his entire leadership. According to all the information we have received yesterday and today, there has been a general mobilisation of Muslim forces in Zenica, where about 8.000 soldiers have been called up and they are now moving towards the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. We are monitoring the situation and it is certain that the Croatian people in Zenica, at least in the part of Zenica where units of the Croatian Defence Council are not strong enough to provide full protection for the Croatian people, we shall give serious consideration to the collective evacuation of the Croatian population from the parts of Zenica which are now under our full control. We shall inform President Boban and the international and European public about this, that the Croats in Zenica, in those parts where they do not feel secure after these murders and after this bloodbath perpetrated by Mujahedin-Muslim forces, that Croats obviously cannot live in those areas under such conditions, and after the continuation of such activities, if they continue, that is, they shall certainly be forced to make this move. We wish to provide full protection to the Croatian population, primarily in Zenica, where units of the Croatian Defence Council, not just from Zenica but from all the territories of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, have the strength to resist a potential aggression and protect the Croats in Zenica. Therefore, we view what has been done as the beginning of an aggression against the Croatian people. "SARIC, HINA: In the last paragraph of the announcement, there is a demand that all Mujahedins be expelled from our territory. Will you insist on this firmly and fully, at what level, and by which means? "DARIO KORDIC: Not only will we insist, but we shall implement this using all available means. Units which are not from this area, that is, who are Mujahedins or who are outside the domicile provinces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, will have to leave this area using all available means. "ZVONIMIR: Zvonimir Cilic, of the Vitez Brigade. Could you please tell me, any one of you, it doesn't matter who, will this long list of atrocities and these terrible pictures be sent to the European Monitoring Mission and UNPROFOR or have they already been delivered to them? "JOURNALIST: Are there any other questions? If not, I would like to ask the Colonel to tell us what is happening in Jablanica and Konjic. "TIHOMIR BLASKIC: I know exactly what is happening, and at 08.00 hours yesterday an order arrived that large-scale attacks were to be made on the Croatian territory of Konjic by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to be specific, by the 4th Corps. The forces brought to this territory to carry out such crimes, who have carried out a large-scale attack, and this attack went on until late last night. In the meantime, we could hear that they glorified that attack, because this was probably a contribution to the celebration of the day of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. At the moment of the forces of the Croatian Defence Council have managed to repulse an attack on the area, especially the area of Jablanica, which is controlled by the Croatian Defence Council, and the defence lines, unfortunately held against us, I say unfortunately, because this kind of combat operations were not our priority, but have evidently been imposed on us, are quite stable, and there will certainly be further operations to protect the Croatian population living in this territory. Concerning the events on the stretch of territory north and northwest of Konjic, I think that eyewitnesses could see the extent of the offensive, where everything is being burned, where the Croatian population is being forcibly evicted, homes are being burned, and those who perhaps stay behind because they cannot move away are disarmed and forced to live under conditions which are below human dignity. We are informed about all the events in Jablanica and Konjic. This shelling went on until late last night, especially the area of Ostrosac, a village in the vicinity of which units of the Croatian Defence Army are located. It has already been said that the time has passed when we could refer to these as incidents, because it is evident that this was a planned attack, an attack primarily on the Croatian people, because it affected villages and areas mostly on the free territory, at least as we see it, where the main forces of the Croatian Defence Council were not present. But in any case, we shall know how to respond to such offensive operations and will respond as the attackers deserve. That is all. "JOURNALIST: Thank you very much. Are there any other questions? If not, thank you very much, and see you on Tuesday."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Witness N, just a few questions about that press conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just one moment. I've got a transcript which continues.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It shouldn't. The balance relates to another tape. I thought it had been cut off. It relates to a later date. We will no doubt come to it on a later occasion. Does it just continue over to the end of the page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It goes over, on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In which case then, everything below the place which we've reached should be either crossed through or even cut off, and we'll deal with it if and when that tape is played.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This press conference, first of all, what time do you recall it being broadcast?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was broadcast in the evening of the 15th, after 20.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning there was film of the incident involving Totic and the killing of the guards. Was the extent of that part of the film, the detail into which it went and the time that it spent dealing with it, typical of broadcasts at that time or was it longer than usual to focus on such matters, or shorter? Tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I noticed in the report that there were no details regarding the officials present carrying out the investigation. However, the method of reporting was typical of that time. All attention focused on the event that took place and all the things that followed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of the broadcast with the various speakers, did you detect any separation of powers, civil from military, in what was said by one speaker or another?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I must object to that question, Your Honour. That --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I agree. Not for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The effect of this broadcast, first of all on you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The effect of this broadcast was frightening, in the sense that until then, in public announcements, such a method of speaking to the public had not been applied. After all, the tone was quieter when reporting on events of this kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's been suggested this was an emergency press conference. What was the frequency of press conferences that were broadcast?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I didn't watch regularly, I think that they were not a daily occurrence but they were held occasionally, these conferences for the press. They were occasionally organised and broadcast on the local media. But normally every evening there were reports on events of the day, but such special press conferences were not a daily occurrence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If and when there were press conferences broadcast, was the lineup of people appearing similar to or different from that which appeared on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I noticed that Mr. Kostroman appeared most frequently, as a rapporteur, at these conferences. Sometimes Kordic, and I forgot to mention a moment ago that Blaskic was present there too. I also mentioned Mr. Cilic, who put one of the questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Mr. Kordic's clothes we could see something of an arm patch. Were you able to see what patch it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the patch of the HVO, the chequerboard sign of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this broadcast, he did not say that the HVO should attack but that they should defend or repel in the interests of the Croatian people. How did that compare with what he generally said on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The usual term used was that they were defending Croatian territories. There was no reference made to capturing other territories, because it was felt that these were territories that needed to be under the control of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Reference to the peoples on one side or another, the Muslim people and the Croat people, as opposed to, for example, specifying the military forces, what effect did that have on you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In such conditions, there were people who helped one another. However, such assistance could be given until personal security became an issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And insofar as the broadcast, the various speakers speak of the peoples on one side and another, rather than the military forces just, or rather than just the military forces. How, if at all, did that affect you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, this press conference affected me in such a way that the reference made to the Bosniak people or the Muslim people in those days, that this address to the Muslim people to renounce their -- I would call it their living areas and life in those areas, because what was happening all the time was something we couldn't understand. That even though we are an old people in those areas, we were always denied our identity and the piece of land which was lawfully Bosniak. Throughout not just this war but before that, the existence of us as a people was challenged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I'm sorry to interrupt, but I think we can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one thing you may be able to help with. The regular reference to "Mujahedin" and "extremists", did you have experience that enabled you to say that that was a fair representation of events or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Once again, I object to that, Your Honour. I think that that calls for a commentary on the evidence and it's a rather vague, nebulously open-ended question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I disagree. I asked him whether he had experience to say whether what was being presented was accurate and fair or otherwise, and if broadcasts are other than accurate and fair, they may have a purpose behind them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness can give evidence of what he saw and observed, and he can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness N, I'll repeat the question. With reference to the "Mujahedin" and "extremists", did you have experience that enabled you to say that what was being said was a fair representation of events or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me say that in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, there were volunteers fighting within the BH army ranks. Those volunteers, and even the section of Muslims who regularly practised their faith, in my personal opinion, were all categorised as "extremists". It was sufficient for somebody to wear a beard, or to pray to God in his own way, for him to be labelled a Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. How many hours after this broadcast were you aware that an attack had taken place on Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The attack occurred in the morning at 5.30 on the 16th, early, at 5.30, and the programme was aired between 8.00 and 9.00 in the evening. So this would mean eight or nine hours after this extraordinary press conference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The uniforms being worn by the people at the press conference, what uniforms were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were standard camouflage uniforms that armies wore in those days. There may have been a shade of difference, I don't know the details, but they were standard camouflage uniforms bearing the insignia of the armies they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The patches that you could see on the other personnel there, could you see any patches on other people at the meeting, or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In passing, and while staying in the village of Ahmici, I saw individuals wearing black uniforms. Later on, after the New Year of 1993, I saw individuals with camouflage uniforms and a leaf on their patch, on their sleeve. These were mostly near the railway station in Stari Vitez and near the Impregnacija plant, at the checkpoint there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, paragraphs 18, 19, and 20 deal with the history of this witness, but I don't think they are going to add to the body of evidence about these topics generally. It's available to be asked about if it falls within the Tribunal's discretion that the matters can be explored, but I don't need to take them from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, we have heard evidence about these matters. Is that all that you want to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, that would be a convenient moment for a further break before cross-examination. Mr. Sayers, I hope that we can deal with all

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now for a quarter of an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might just pass out for the Court and for the Prosecution and co-defendants the introduction that was given to the press conference which was part of the Kupreskic exhibit, and also the memorandum that I referred to containing the Translation Unit's views on the translation issue I earlier raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I take it the tape was Exhibit 665; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And the transcripts 665,1, 2, and 3. This can be attached -- and there's no dispute about this, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What would be a suitable number for this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The sensible thing would really be to make the first part of it part of 665,3 -- in fact, why don't we make it all part of 665,3, if that's not going to cause the Registry difficulties, rather than give it a separate number. But if it is going to create difficulty, then let it be 665,3-1, whatever is most convenient for the Registry, for their logging of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may be most convenient, 665,3-1. We will all remember where it in fact goes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Witness N, good morning. My name is Stephen Sayers. I'm one of the attorneys representing Dario Kordic. Over to my left here are the attorneys representing Mario Cerkez. Let me begin by asking you a few, and only a few, general questions, sir. As I understand it, sir, there are four separate production factories in the town of Vitez. The first is the Vitezit factory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that factory manufactures, amongst other things, industrial and military explosives; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Industrial explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. The second factory is the Sintevit factory; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that, I believe, concentrates upon the manufacture of plastics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Then we have a rather larger institution, more diversified institution, called the Slobodan Princip Seljo factory; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And one of the things that this factory manufactures is nitroglycerine-based gunpowder that is required for artillery rounds and also infantry ammunition; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And then the final production facility is the Impregnacija facility. I'm not clear what that factory actually manufactures. Could you please tell the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Impregnacija company was not part of this company. It was a facility that did with -- worked with wood. It was lumber, parquet floors, and it was also impregnated railroad ties and telephone and telegraph poles, things like that. But it was not part of that same complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In other words, it had no military function?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Impregnacija did not have a military function, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You have talked about the elections that were held in 1990. They were followed by, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, by the secession from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia of the countries of Croatia and Slovenia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We do not call it "secession." We say that the population, through the elections, voted for its own state. We never use the word "secession."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness N. It would be fair to say, though, that the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the Socialist Federal Republic, was essentially in a state of disintegration by the middle of 1991 and early 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, the elections led to a civilian government in Vitez, and as I understand it, the president of the municipality was Ivica Santic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ivica Santic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would you describe him as the most prominent Croat politician in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And his colleagues, I believe, were Pero Skopljak, amongst others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pero Skopljak, Anto Valenta, and some others. I couldn't [sic] name them too, because I'm from Vitez, so I know quite a few people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, the people that we've just mentioned, were any of those in the HVO, the military arm, if you like, of the Croat authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, it was usual for people to wear camouflage uniforms, so I cannot say precisely yes or no, but occasionally they would wear camouflage uniforms with the HVO insignia. I am not familiar with the later organisation, so what certain individuals did by wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You would agree that just because you happened to be attired in a uniform during this period, 1992 and 1993, did not necessarily mean that you were actually in the military forces; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But all announcements or pronouncements were accompanied by the HVO signature, and to me, that symbolised the military -- or this military component of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I understand, sir, but the question that I asked you is a little bit more general than that. Just because someone was wearing a uniform or seen in a uniform -- or camouflage clothing, to be more accurate -- during this period of time did not necessarily mean that that person was in the armed forces on either side, because basically that was the normal type of clothing that you expected to see people in, in everyday life; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could say it that way too, because we did not know details.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Let me just turn your attention to a specific period about which there has been some discussion, and I don't think that the precise chronology of events is yet clear. I would like to clear it up with you, if I can. In the early summer of 1992, would you agree that this was a time of great chaos and confusion in Bosnia-Herzegovina generally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You wouldn't? All right. Wouldn't you agree that a state of an imminent threat of war had been declared by President Izetbegovic on April the 9th of 1992, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This was only one month after the referendum, or actually one month after the formal declaration of the independent Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And as we all know, the capital of the country, Sarajevo, had been surrounded by Bosnian Serb forces which were launching a violent military attack upon the capital and besieging it; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, the Trial Chamber knows that the HVO authorities assumed control of the local government in Vitez on the 20th of June, 1992. Is that broadly consistent with your recollection, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is how it was. This is how it was. You have somewhere the exact date. It must be written down somewhere. I just know that it was sometime in late June. I know that the legally elected Bosniak representatives, from that date on, were forbidden to enter the municipal building, and there was a document which they were supposed to sign. If they signed it, they were allowed to enter the building, those who had signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. It was actually the date of June the 20th that I was concentrating upon, because I want you to agree with me that that was the date upon which President Izetbegovic actually declared that a state of war existed in your country; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether those two dates are identical. I did not keep a journal, so I did not make any entries which I would be able to check to see whether those two dates were identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just to establish this point, may it please the Court, I'd like to have one exhibit marked, which is an order issued on June the 20th of 1992, an order of general mobilisation. I would also like the witness to be shown Exhibit D17-1,2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Sayers, before we do that, I wonder if there's much point in this. This witness has not, in fact, given any great evidence, if at all, about the background. The evidence which he's given has really concentrated merely on the presentation of the video and events about that time. I note that these are questions which you have asked other witnesses, and I wonder if there is a great deal of point in going over this particular matter with witness after witness. What I have in mind is this: that you can call your own evidence on this particular topic. We will have a chance of comparing such evidence as there has been, but I don't think it's really taking us much further to argue these points with particular witnesses, especially when they haven't dealt in any detail with the background. So shall we move on?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'm entirely in agreement with Your Honour. I wanted to establish that particular point, because I do not believe that particular point has been established by the evidence yet. I don't think there's dispute about it and I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Witness N, it is true that you actually never lost your job before the outbreak of hostilities on April the 16th, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, turning to the authorities in Vitez, who actually was the head of the HDZ party in Vitez in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first it was Mr. Ivica Santic, and after him it was Pero Skopljak. I'm not sure about Anto Valenta, because I was not a member of the party. I was not in meetings where I would get in touch with any of the officials, so I only know of Ivica Santic and Pero Skopljak having been the leaders of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Would it be fair to say then that you don't really know very much about the internal organisation and the actual offices that people held within the HDZ BiH party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know many details. In my testimony, I mentioned events which I experienced firsthand. As to the background of these events, there are many other witnesses who know much more about this, those who were members in the SDS or HDZ and other parties, and who, by being in all these meetings, would be able to deal in much more depth with these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And the same answer, I take it, sir, goes for your knowledge of the HVO and also the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. You don't really know, yourself, about too many details, and who held what post and when; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know who was president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in those days; it was Mate Boban. I know that at first the headquarters -- the focus was on the protection of cultural values, language, and other such things, for in those days, the Muslims too had activated their society, Merhamet. Then there was Preporod by the Serb side. This was their cultural society. While there were discussions on cultural matters, there were no conflicts; but the moment the discussions turned to the state organisation of Herceg-Bosna, then the problems arose which we are dealing with here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me just mention one of the comments that was made by Mr. Kordic, on page 21 of the transcript that has been marked as Exhibit Z665.1. Mr. Kordic is referring to terrible agony in the Konjic municipality. Did you know that Konjic had been attacked on April 14th by Muslim forces, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not prone to use the term "attack". In my testimony, I use words saying that throughout the federation of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina there were conflicts where the HDZ had majority rule, and on that basis, he wanted to organise everything from the economy, the people, everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In connection with the comments that were made by Mr. Kordic, he goes on to say that: "The government of the Croatian Defence Council had sent a clear message to everyone at its special meeting yesterday." Who was the head of the government of the Croatian Defence Council, sir, do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Who was the head of the government of the Croatian Defence Council, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For a time -- you mean Herceg-Bosna or Vitez? In Vitez it was Ivica Santic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You've already said that, and I think you've already identified who the head of the HZ-HB was, so let me move on. You were a member of the coordination committee for the protection of Muslims, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There were 18 members on that committee, one of whom was Sefkija Dzidic; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. Dzidic had actually replaced Mr. Cengic as commander of territorial defence forces before the blockade incident on October the 19th and 20th, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Before the blockade incident that I have just mentioned, the headquarters of the Territorial Defence forces was actually at the Boris Kidric High School in Vitez; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And after the barricade incident, that headquarters was relocated to Stari Vitez, initially in the house of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If I may write this down, Your Honour, and have it shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You gave some evidence concerning an order that had supposedly been issued by a gentleman named Bozo Rajic. It's true, is it not, sir, that Mr. Rajic was the Minister of Defence of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you know that Mr. Rajic was also a vice-president of the HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that detail. I wasn't following so closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. I didn't follow your evidence regarding when you saw this order, but let me suggest to you that the order was issued, if at all, in January of 1993. Is that consistent with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my statement, I didn't say I had seen the order, but that at the meeting held in October, reference was made to the uniting of the BH army and the HVO in territories where the HDZ had legally won the majority in those municipalities. However, I didn't see the written instructions, because I was not a member of any such bodies where this would be viewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Then that need not detain us very long, sir. Let me move on to the next subject. You touched briefly upon the first incident of conflict that broke out between armed forces of the HVO and the Territorial Defence in your municipality, and that occurred on October the 19th or 20th, 1992. Do you remember that? That's correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that an HVO troop convoy headed westward was stopped at gunpoint by forces of the Territorial Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It was not stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. It wasn't stopped by the Territorial Defence. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. By whom was it stopped then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That convoy was stopped because in those days, massive layoffs were being done of Bosniaks in Impregnacija and other companies, and it was customary for there to be roadblocks at every 500 to 1.000 metres, and then a group of people from Ahmici had set up this roadblock. As far as I know, in this conflict, which was not a very fierce one, because it was probably halted on time, I don't know by whom, so that a couple of houses were damaged. I don't know whether anyone was injured or killed that evening because immediately after that conflict, we went to the village of Ahmici and spoke to the villagers, asking them to calm things down and that such things should not happen again. We even jointly organised the repairing of damaged houses by polling our efforts and funds.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And the explanation for the barricade, that you've just given, was that, broadly speaking, the view of all of your colleagues on the coordination committee for the protection of Muslims, as far as you can tell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regarding the barricade?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not attend any meeting at which instructions were given to build a roadblock.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You have never heard that those instructions were actually issued by General Hadzihasanovic in Zenica, from the headquarters of the 3rd Corps, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard later that it was Hadzihasanovic who had actually issued instructions not to put up barricades. It was because of that that the problem had arisen, the fact that this had happened in this village in such a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Five or six days after the barricade incident, you actually participated in negotiations with local residents of the village of Ahmici and representatives?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's said that he did. Again, we've heard much evidence about this barricade and the events relating to it. I wonder if we really need go over it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Only one point that I was interested in covering that I do not believe has been covered with previous witnesses, if it pleases the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask you two questions on this. You actually spoke at the house of Ivo Papic, did you not, and there were discussions between him, a man named Kupreskic spoke up, along with a man by the name of Fuad Berbic as well; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. May I explain a little?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is there any particular point to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The second question was: Basically, what you were trying to do is to get an agreement between all the local residents of Ahmici that they wouldn't fight each other in the future; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's the only issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you want to add anything to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no need to add because the names were mentioned. Vlatko Kupreskic was mentioned, Ivo Papic. So there's no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Moving on in time to January of 1993, you and your colleagues formed a war presidency in Vitez at that time, is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The war presidency was formed but not by me, because I wasn't in the executive board of the party. I said that there was a misinterpretation there in my statement, because I wasn't a member of the executive board of the party or a member of the party at all. It was the executive board of the party that formed the war presidency at the beginning of January or the end of December, and from that moment when the presidency was formed, then the executive board was elected among the legally-elected Bosniaks who had stayed behind, and that is when that body started to function.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You were actually a member of the war presidency itself, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were not. All right. Let me ask you: Your focus, if you like, is really on the municipality of Vitez. Did you hear that fighting had broken out, towards the end of January, in the adjoining municipality of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had heard of the conflicts in Busovaca, in Novi Travnik, in Stupni Do, later Ovnak, and all these things. In those days, there was information provided regarding many events that took place at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It would be fair to say, though, that because you lived in an adjoining municipality, you didn't really know any details concerning the fighting that had broken out in Busovaca in January of 1993? That would be say to say, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know the details. I knew that fighting had broken out as a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It would be equally fair to say, sir, that you really did not know very much about the municipal government of the municipality of Busovaca, who held what post or when, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That didn't even interest me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You heard, on the press conference that you were asked to sit through, comments made by all of the speakers regarding acts perpetrated by Muslim extremists. You didn't condone, yourself, any of the acts of these extremists, such as the one that was shown right at the beginning of the tape, with those four people riddled with bullets, you didn't condone that kind of action, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you followed closely, I said that it was customary to speak of incidents on both sides, and it was customary for both sides to justify their moves in military terms. The reasons can be given by the gentleman from the military who participated in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That would be Colonel Blaskic, I take it, insofar as this particular --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Blaskic and Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let's me turn to the part of the conference which Mr. Kordic addressed. He didn't utter any threats of initiating attacks on the Muslim people, and he never did when you saw him on press conferences. Isn't that a true statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic didn't say something in so many words, but the tone he used, for me, was unusual. The tone of that announcement at the press conference, and in view of everything that was going on, in my statement I conveyed my thoughts as to how I thought about it at the time. Let me repeat a saying that we use in Bosnia. It didn't smell of good things to come. It didn't bode well for the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You gave a statement first on February the 28th, 1995, and July the 15th, 1995, to the investigators helping the Prosecution, and you said, on page 5, that: "Mr. Kordic did not say that the HVO should attack but the HVO must defend the interests of the Croatian people. He always said this on television." Now, that's a truthful statement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was stated in my testimony here too, but it is well known that official announcements and concrete acts in practice did not coincide, nor were they, let me say, identical or synchronised.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, we've all seen the videotape of the press conference, and we've all seen the demeanour of the people at this press conference. I think that you would agree that Mr. Kordic's style was fairly calm and rational, and that's consistent with the demeanour that you saw him demonstrate at other press conferences throughout 1993, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His style was not pacifying, in my view.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, you never saw him on the television ranting and raving and pounding the table, so to speak, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That depends on the temperament of the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But you never saw Mr. Kordic, on the TV programmes that you saw, the press conferences and so forth, you never saw him demonstrate a demeanour that was significantly different from what we saw today, did you, calm, rational, not angry? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my statement, I said that I watched those conferences only rarely. When there was a line-up of the brigade in Vitez, I wasn't present at the stadium, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, Witness N, let me just interrupt. You said that you saw Mr. Kordic occasionally on press conferences, and what I'd like you to agree to is this, that he was never other than you saw him on this particular press conference: calm, rational, not angry, self-contained; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I saw among the conferences, he used a sharp tone, but he didn't bang his fist on the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. At page 22 of the transcript, Colonel Blaskic referred to having informed the chief of the main staff in Mostar about what was going on. Do you know who the chief of the HVO general staff in Mostar was, sir? I know that you've said you're not a military man.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You mentioned Anto Valenta during your testimony, and you made a reference to a book that Mr. Valenta had written. That book was written, actually, before the referendum that was held in early 1992; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The book was written in fact in 1991, and it expressed his own personal views, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I read it, knowing Anto Valenta as an engineer of technology who never studied history and geography, it was a surprise for me that Mr. Valenta should have written such a book.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Did you know that Mr. Valenta had actually never held any office in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time, I knew that he had a position in a hierarchy other than the municipal hierarchy, but which one, I don't know, whether he was in the main board or something like that. But I know that he held some sort of a position at a higher level than the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
